messages.subject: poppr beginner
messages.body_plain:
Hello

I am a beginner in R and I want to calculate the index of association by poppr for each of the population within the SNPs dataset (attached). It is derived a csv sheet prepared for genalex.

I installed the poppr package in R but could not load the file (e.g. LL_snp_CADM.csv) into the software. Do you have any suggestions on the input file format? or command line?
 e.g. >- read.genalex or data()

 If I cam able to load the file, then I can use the command ia .... (on manual p. 27) to calculate the index. Am I right? I will appreciate your comments.

Many thanks,
regards,
KM

messages.subject: Re: poppr beginner
messages.body_plain:
Hi KM,

>From the format of your file, the easiest way to read in your data would be to use the function read.csv <http://www.cyclismo.org/tutorial/R/input.html#reading-a-csv-file> to load the data into R and then the function df2genind <http://adegenet.r-forge.r-project.org/files/tutorial-basics.pdf> (see section 4.2 of the adegenet basics tutorial) to convert it to a genind object.

Note that for your data set, you have the sample names in column 1 and the population names in column 2, so you will need to use some subsetting (here's a tutorial <http://www.ats.ucla.edu/stat/r/modules/subsetting.htm>).

Here's some example code:

snps.df <- read.csv("GC_snp_CADM.csv", head = FALSE, sep = ",")
# note that I'm telling read.csv that the file has no column names with head = FALSE

snps <- df2genind(snps.df[, -c(1, 2)], ind.names = snps.df[[1]], pop = snps.df[[2]], ploidy = 1)
# Change the ploidy to whatever you need

poppr(snps)
# Calculate index of association and basic summary statistics

Hope that helps,
Zhian
